PROLOGUE

The dry air of Nekamtol possessed a warm taste of open casks and staled brew, when I came to face her across the table. Scents of beer and liquor still wafted up from half-filled mugs and glasses upon the wood, their stains of condensation soaking against the polished fibers which held them up. As if weapons, the ware was left strewn about as though the hall itself was a field of a battle that long since passed. Those many worn pieces of glass and stone watched on with haunting gazes; memorials of a final moment where graves stood missing only the flocks of ravens that might caw and flock among them.

Many years had flown past beneath this roof, and within this hall. Those ages had come and gone with only the perceived trickle of days and moments among such great currents of time, yet it seemed they had been moving too quickly for my mind to hold and truly possess. Thick windows of glass above our heads could not hope to illuminate the power of this place. Under the protection of its thick keep made from wood and stone, we had celebrated countless victories and mourned many defeats; planned and plotted adventures that would take us far beyond what any others might aspire to tread. From the spoils of glory and triumph resting heavily on spokes of iron, to the scuffs upon the planked wood floor. This hall was now a tomb.

I kept silent as our eyes met, and that pained expression of sorrow and guilt crushed whatever resistance I might hope to muster against it. For her, for them: In my mind, in that moment, a battle was fought and waged against the passing of time itself. A war and campaign hopelessly lost in the crushing passage of seconds. For in the instant she bowed, submitting the final blow of defeat; A blow wrapped as deeply in respect as one might ever hope to find, delivered by a being of beauty: It was over.

"I won't forget you, John." Her voice was barely a whisper, wrapped in green cloth of silk and fern, to which the colors caught even in the darkness. The quiet echo of her voice lifted over the hushed wood like a cool wind, ushered to my ears beneath the trophies of uncountable victories and heroic deeds. â€œI won't forget what you did for me. For all of us.â€

Together, She and I were the last. Around us the chains of rank and name lay still, medallions quietly hanging where they had been left upon empty chairs.

"I won't forget you either, Elise." My voice caught on that reply, sinking slowly in my chest. In the shadows of the dim room, my face held at bay whatever twisted expression of sadness it wished for, desperate for dignity as I spoke once more. "I won't forget any of you."

Her tan face and thin lips pulled into a smile, single scar along her left cheek creasing as pale hands lifted the thin chain from her neck, silver and steel slowly drawing along with tiny clinks of metal. She dropped the pieces lightly on the chair while she stood, hands clenched, draping the coils along until the pieces held taunt: Fixed and secure against gravity and time.

Those soft palms held there against the wood, pressing it in as her mind fell into deeper thoughts, quiet and reflective. When she did speak again, the words came slowly, with true finality. "May the sun forever shine upon your face, and may Justice be always found where you are near."

Our Guild's Creed, given voice by the one who created it all those years ago. Before the others, before the journeys, the battles, the defeats and the triumphs: Back when there were simply two friends traveling out together into the great unknown. I knew I was crying, but she didn't see me. Her own eyes were blinded by the same.

"Goodbye John."

There was no ceremony. No flash of brilliance to show what she had been, or what I had known her to be. For all her great deeds, the heroic acts, and the beauty she had brought to this world. No, when she disappeared, Elise simply did not exist any longer. She was gone. For all the proof of my truest and most trusted friend in this world, there was only a chain of metal draped upon an empty seat. "Goodbye Elise."

I was alone.

Chapter 1

After the accident, what began as a simple question twisted into an obsession. A endless repetition, I couldn't help but listen to while it echoed onward without answer; over and over again. No matter how much time passed, or however much I tried to turn away and focus elsewhere: While I lay in that helpless state, that single question haunted my thoughts. Why did I stay in this place?

Years flew by, yet for all the days spent pondering as my injuries bent the existence I lead into a husk of my previous life, I could never find a better answer than the absence of choice. Over and over again, my thoughts smashed against a wall I was unable to surpass, and in such there was finality. Life was completely lacking alternatives, and all that it gave in return was a curse of bittersweet flavor that I could not escape. As time move forward, even the world itself seemed to reeked of that terrible stench.

No hidden gems or lost knowledge remained in this place, and nothing of value had been left for me to find regardless of how long I might choose to continue the search. If it truly was exploration and freedom I craved from within the living corpse my mind possessed, such ages and adventures had past long before I had arrived to consider their significance. The beauty and wonder of the globe were already burned away, thousands of years before my soul found itself trapped upon this surface. Those had belonged to the ancestors of my ancestors, and then ended with them.

If there was a choice: Why not leave?

Though I searched in vain for the genuine option that I hoped and prayed might be hidden, I could never find a true escape. Even in the age of potential in which I found myself, reality was harsh and uncaring to those stuck within its grasp. As it was, I settled with the only viable option of trickery. A drug for the mind alone; of false and detailed illusions toward a sole purpose of forgetting that colder truth.

Artificial and constructed dreams made real; to live among what you choose, as you choose. The realm in which I fled was a Virtual reality. In concept, such ideas had been thought of long ago, perhaps in the beginning no more than simple fantasy. As a dream that many had wanted and wished for, it persisted if only by fanatic delusion, but like my own unforgiving and haunting questions: For some rare few it became an obsession that spanned generations.

Hundreds of years carried the potential onward from thought to construction. Yet for all the great minds who had attempted to bring it into existence, none had ever quite managed in perfection. There was just so much to cover just among the senses of sight, smell, taste, touch, and sound. These fundamental pieces that make up reality had needed to be constructed anew by the millions. Then there were also the lesser senses- those of attributes often overlooked: Feelings of gravity and temperature, pain and pleasure, hunger or thirst. How many others had there been, lurking in the background unknown to those who possessed them until confronted with their absence?

All these had to be understood and perfected, each generation of great minds picking up the work of their predecessors and carrying it to further heights. Even in the world and era I came to know as the age of Enhanced, how long did it take for this level of realness to finally be reached? What manner of time and effort had been placed as a sacrifice on the altar of delusion? Although those years and lives had my utmost gratitude, truth be told it didn't matter in the slightest to me how long it had been. What efforts had transpired were taken for granted. I came after its completion, just like everything else in this world. With no work or effort of my own that ancient history was my inheritance as well as my curse.

My birthright was to stumble upon this realization, and in doing so: My long sought choice, however false it was.

I left the old world behind and stepped into the new without hesitation. Reduced my life and existence to a small cube no larger than a closet by appearances. In this space lay the deep immersion pod, nestled snug against three walls. A model of the longest-lasting and most capable variety: Complete with sustenance and filtered gel to sustain even the most excessive of deep-syncs, more capable than another other in existence upon its purchase.

In this capsule, I had given up my rights to life beyond those four walls. I gave up the world outside, and locked myself away within the that cocoon. For all the time I had lived in that old world of technology, money, greed and stale air: It was long enough. I had taken what was needed from it, extracting the one manifestation of its great wonders which might hold a true value for my life.

The technology was a powerful. Far beyond any one person's comprehension. God only knows how lives were wasted on its creation and perfection, for I stood upon the shoulders of Giants in the clouds not willing to look the long way down below. To know it was there at all, was enough. To know and experience what the machine was capable of, was enough.

A gateway for the mind was opened wide, within the capsule and the flood of bio-gel. There was a door for my mind to pass through: A means to go and live a different life in a different place far from the tainted skies of gray, or the crushing essence of urban expansions and pressing greed.

Far from the things I hated, it took me to a new world: Where the Guild has grown around me. Where strangers turned to friends, turned to family. Where monsters roamed, Humanity fought, and legends were made from flesh and blood. A place I had hoped to live until the end, if only.

Now it was ending. One by one those servers would go dark, reality spinning off into silence, towns and cities crumbling beneath the absolute nothingness, left empty of their brilliance. If I were to awaken from this world, and be forced back into the reality that lay beyond it, what would become of me?

Returning to the world of my birth, a place that had never once welcomed me with anything greater than a passing indifference. The thought sickened me to my core, dread seeping in like black sludge along my mind. I still couldn't walk, I could barely lift my arms. The accident had left me a husk of what I'd once been, and no amount of wishing or sobbing could bring me back to normal. The only place I could feel alive, was here. The New World. To even consider going back, to try and start anew in a different reality similar to this one I must soon leave behind...

No, even with such a possibility I couldn't bear the thought of leaving. This was where I was free, where I was truly alive: But in five minutes... No, four now... In Three minutes and fifty seven seconds, my world would end.

My world would end.

With a heavy sigh, my legs pushed from the chair of wood I had rested and I turned to look at what remained, bearing witness to the empty hall that had once been so full of life. The Building was empty around me, fifty seats bearing only their silent memorial of chains. Those medallions of metal and plate caught the slender drafts of morning light not yet truly cresting the Eastern Mountains, a my own came to lay among the rest.

No ceremony worthy of it by any means, but with none to witness but myself I supposed that no ceremony was required. If any in this world could claim to possess the knowledge, it was I alone what knew what significance that necklace of silver and plate held. That was what mattered in the end, and it was the end, after all: This was it for me and for the world I stood.

00 Days: 00 Hours: 02 Minutes: 37 Seconds

A subtle tension of my thoughts brought to focus the logs of interface within my mind's eye, bringing the timer atop a screen in my vision. It slowly settled down in silence as the ever-growing impulse to run pressed at my mind, pressing down with the increasing weight. A primal and pointless sensation of terror gripping at the rational thoughts which governed my actions, as if I might escape the countdown by fleeing. Try as I did to quell them, the urge to sprint as fast as I could, to channel all my power and let my legs carry me off into the horizon and far from the troubles that followed me, did not settle as I hoped.

I tried to reason with myself.

Where would I go- Out into the streets? What purpose could that possibly bring me? Running away from the end of the world seemed more than just highly impractical. As if I could hope to achieve anything by sprinting past the curious faces of this city's Non-player characters. In my mind's eye I could imagine outrunning their many scripted questions, letting them trail behind while I fled without purpose or direction.

Just the thought of it brought a bitter smile to my face. If they truly had the minds to understand it, I wonder if those characters walking among the streets of Nekamtol might run with me. If they knew, same as I: That the world is about to end, not with a bang, but with a whisper. That the universe of reality itself is about to be pulled out like a rug beneath their feet, and nothing but empty black would remain. Nothing.

That long fought terror seized me in greater force than I'd anticipated, and before I knew, I truly was running.

Doors of the Guild hall slammed behind me with a thundering crash, and the expected shouts and voices of surprise from those I passed soared by my head with questions and fear so real it was almost enough to break me from my panic. The people of this world had always been so genuine, so real. That had always made the city feel safe, beautiful even: But now it only added to the despair. I didn't look back at their faces as I ran onward.

00 Days: 00 Hours: 00 Minutes: 50 Seconds

My feet had cleared the mud and dirt, throwing them aside to enter cobblestones. Rough and solid rock beneath boots that pressed back with every bit of force I could hammer into them. The leather and bindings taking the weight of my frame with soft creaks, as the sword clattered- held in place to my side even by a practiced hand as I sprinted towards the higher city.

"You there! Stop or cease!" A city-guard shouted at me as I shouldered past him, pressing onto the stairs that would take me upward, higher. I had to go higher, to the battlements of the wall: To watch the sun rise one last time over the Great Bastion of Nekamtol, To witness the final seconds of this world in all their glory.

00 Days: 00 Hours: 00 Minutes: 10 Seconds

Panting, I cleared the final pitch, stairs twisting around the turn of the tower's form to step out onto the high-rise and face the east. Red stone beneath my feet caught the light, draping deep shadows behind the parapets that extended on its outer edge as the haze of morning sunk down from the sky above.

There it was.

Distant form like dragon's teeth, the Eastern Mountains held together along the horizon as the light lifted behind them: A breath of flame whose heat reached out to touch the expanse beyond. My face prickled with the sensation, even in the chill wind of the high wall. Here, in this place I might see it all. From the mountains, the fields the clouded draft of the Southern ocean of tears. Behind my shoulders rose the Royal towers, and beyond them in the West was the Great Forest.

For all the memories, in all of its glory: All I could do was bear silent witness to the world that had taken me in when I had nothing left. The timer fell away as I counted down unassisted, forcing my eyes open to the last.

Five seconds.

Four Seconds.

Three Seconds.

Two Seconds.

One.

Zero.

The air lifted, rising high under the heat of the sun, rooftops of the lower city now illuminated with soft hues of green and red stone, copper and sands. A Monastery bell ran out, soft chimes holding to the wind as I held there, disbelieving the reality around me. I was still here? Slowly, my mind reach out, checking for the logs- ready to confirm the obvious. Was the game- the world, still online? Was this simply a moment's limbo waiting for the dark? No logs or data-screens appeared in my mind's eye as I reached for them. No mappings, explanations, or windows of text could be found. Staring at my hands, I felt them close firmly against the battlement's stone edge, thick granite roughly textured to a cool touch beneath my skin. As real as if ever was, if not more; but I knew it would end in an instant. Any second now this world would cease forever, and even if there had been some delay or glitch, I couldn't let this moment be ruined in my mind. I wanted- needed, to focus and embrace until it was firmly locked into my memory. Footsteps and exhausted panting came into the background, echoing slightly off the hollow tower and stairs behind me. The rough gasps of a tired soul overshadowed the clank of metal armor pieces.

"Stop-Haa... Stop, or Cease Trespasser!" The Guard's voice was haggard, as he pressed out onto the rounded balcony of the battlement. I turned, eyes wide as he stepped closer- armor immaculate with the colors of Nekamtol's Royal guard. He was breathing heavily, shoulders shifting in uneven motions as his posture fought to right itself.

Was that Normal?

"Stop there, or I'll- haa.” He heaved once more, before stepping forward. “I'll be forced to arrest you!" The Guard stared at me with stern eyes and a sweaty face, and I stared at him astonished. I'd never seen this kind of behavior before, not from an NPC. Slowly, his gaze narrowed a a hand sword reached towards the blade at his hip. The frown on his face seemed peculiar, detailed beyond familiarity- and yet still he did not draw as I normally would have expected.

I had to ask myself again, as curiosity began muddying the waters of my mind further still to a clouded confusion: Was that normal? As we stared at one another, In that instant I felt clarity. On the wind there were the scents of sweat, of cloth and leather. I could feel the exhaustion in my calves from the stairs I'd run only a short while ago, and taste the flow of pollen from the Royal orchards; sharp and sweet aroma of apples among cool air. More than that though, I could sense a nagging realization that something was different. As if the world was suddenly off and wrong compared to the moment before.

Like when you're walking down a dark road on a dark night, and there are eyes piercing into your shoulders that send chills along your spine. When you know in an instant that everything around you is all too real, but you just can't put a finger on why it matters- only that it does. I opened my mouth to speak, just as he drew his sword.
